purpose: Synthetic finite-algorithm and numerical-bound verification only; no calibration-effect experiment

noisy_audit_30000.certificate_scope: Numerically guarded objective bound; not directed-rounding proof, positional uniqueness, or localization accuracy

mathematical_audit.rectangle: For each receiver, distance lies between exact rectangle nearest/farthest distances. Positive n makes residual monotone in distance. Squared-residual interval minimum is zero if residual straddles zero, otherwise nearer endpoint squared. Sum is a valid mathematical lower bound even when individual minima cannot occur together.
mathematical_audit.exterior: Reverse triangle inequality gives distance >= R-||a_i|| for ||x||>=R. Positive residual lower bounds alone contribute squared lower bounds; negative lower residual permits zero. For n>0 all residual lower bounds diverge with R; doubling eventually excludes an improving exterior in exact arithmetic.
mathematical_audit.square: The square [-R,R]^2 covers the ball. Every point outside the square is outside the ball, whose objective already exceeds the incumbent. A numerical lower bound over the square therefore supports a whole-plane objective gap under the stated floating-point caveat.
mathematical_audit.precision: nextafter and explicit guards are conservative checks, not formal directed-rounding interval arithmetic. Bound sampling is a regression check, not a proof of floating-point correctness.
mathematical_audit.solver_scope: Fixed finite algorithm; endpoints include nonconverged finite results, and finite starting points survive failures. Minimum objective is not positional accuracy or uniqueness.
mathematical_audit.scaling: Production uses M+9 local starts and at most 200 residual evaluations per start; analytic Jacobians cost O(M). Stronger audit uses M+25 starts at 1000 evaluations, then at most B splits, each with two O(M) bounds/objectives and heap O(log B); retained rectangle storage O(B).
